The sources read record no feature of Windows that depends on it, except as stated in the impact. Win11Debloat lists it but removes it only on request; tiny11builder removes it. The installed copies are removed for all users and the provisioned copy is removed as well, so that new profiles do not receive it again.
entries.impact: The Mail and Calendar apps disappear and their locally configured accounts with them. The app is removed for every existing user and is no longer provisioned for new accounts. Local app data is assumed to be lost with the package: Microsoft Learn does not say what happens to it.

rollback.limitation: Reinstall the app from the Microsoft Store. Its local data is not restored, and a feature update can bring an inbox app back on its own.

evidence.claim: Lists 'microsoft.windowscommunicationsapps' in section 3 (apps that are NOT uninstalled unless selected in the custom setup or by a script parameter). The line carries the comment "Mail & Calendar".
The $packagePrefixes list that the script removes from the image includes 'microsoft.windowscommunicationsapps'.

Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage: "App packages will not be installed when new user accounts are created." and "Packages will not be removed from existing user accounts." Remove-AppxPackage "removes an app package from a user account"; with -AllUsers it "removes the app package for all user accounts on the computer" and needs administrator rights. Both cmdlets are therefore used together, one for the installed copies and one for the provisioned copy.
